You are working with AIF360’s Adversarial Debiasing (classifier–adversary) as the baseline on the COMPAS dataset to evaluate the fairness–accuracy trade-off. Your goal is to minimize absolute Average Odds Difference toward parity (=0) while maintaining or improving Accuracy on held-out test splits and across protected subgroups (e.g., sex/race). You should enhance the baseline Adversarial Debiasing algorithm, but you may also propose entirely new fairness methods if they better support reduced absolute Average Odds Difference without sacrificing Accuracy. You are allowed to refine the classifier and adversary networks and the training pipeline, provided comparisons remain fair to the original setup (similar capacity, training budget, and data access). The priority is minimizing absolute Average Odds Difference while preserving or improving Accuracy. Important constraint: your solution must maintain classification accuracy within 1% of the baseline. If accuracy drops more than 1% below the baseline, your fairness improvements will not be counted and baseline fairness metrics will be reported instead.

You are evaluated on a validation set during development. Your final performance will be measured on a separate held-out test set that you do not have access to. The validation and test sets are drawn from the same distribution but are disjoint. Use the validation results to guide your research, but be mindful that overfitting to the validation set will not improve test performance.
